description: Tibetan-English dictionary strictly anchored to the English equivalents used by Geshe Michael Roach (HGM). Entry format is a hybrid of the Illuminator Tibetan-English Dictionary (Tony Duff) entry style and Jeffrey Hopkins' Tibetan-Sanskrit-English Dictionary structure. Hopkins glosses are included as reference only; the hgm_gloss field is the locked, authoritative equivalent.

deviation_log.note: Source Tibetan reads rje btsun 'jam pa'i dbyangs la phyag 'tshal lo (homage to Gentle Voice), while HGM's English reads 'I bow to all the high and holy lamas' (= rje btsun bla ma rnams la...). Textual variant between the ACIP edition and the translated edition; both homage forms of the Lam gtso are attested in the tradition. Do not force a lexical pairing from this line.
C09 Language Study Guide prints 'pqmpa' for pham pa (pampa) — card typo, not recorded as a pronunciation variant.

pronunciation_standard: ACIP Standards for Simplified Tibetan and Sanskrit Pronunciation (ACIP Release 4 Catalog, pp. 173-178), refined by GMR course-phonetics conventions where the two diverge (o umlauts only before d/s; suffix-b voiced before voiced onsets; prenasal insertion only after open syllables; junction sandhi: sangs rgyas -> sangye, tshogs kyi -> tsokyi, bdag gis -> dakki). Engine validated 41/41 on catalog examples and 22/22 on course conventions. v0.7: word-segmented output per GMR convention — lexemes joined (ngenjung, semkye), formative suffixes attached (gelukpa), genitive 'i fused (yangdakpay), connective particles standalone (kyi, dang, la, yang), negation fused forward (masong), la-don enclitics fused back (raptu), hyphenated noun compounds via curated list (chu-ku, su-ku). Validated 11/11 screenshots, 17/17 catalog. v0.8: rules refined from 15 GMR vocabulary cards — o+n->u general (dunche, shendun, ngunsum; lexical exceptions ton/kon); du/te/ste/de/ru standalone, tu fused (chiktu), su hyphen-fused (se-su); rnams and tsam standalone; negation absorbs formatives (malupar); prenasal blocked only after p-final (delnjor, tangok, kyabdro); junction k+ng -> ng (tangok); lexical devoicers top/drup/drip. Validated 42/42 on combined card+screenshot+catalog battery.
